title: Interactions of sleep oscillations and synaptic scaling processes across NREM-REM sleep states in healthy aging: a combined experimental-computational approach
summary: While we sleep, our brain sorts new memories and transfers them from short-term to long-term memory. Various brain waves work together in this process: slow waves during deep sleep and fast sleep spindles coordinate this transfer. At the same time, unnecessary neural connections are weakened so that the brain can regain its balance. Dream sleep (REM sleep) in particular seems to recalibrate the relationship between excitatory and inhibitory signals. The planned study uses targeted brain stimulation and computer models to investigate how the various sleep phases interact during this nocturnal reorganization process in healthy older adults and in epilepsy patients with intracranially implanted electrodes. The aim is to understand how the brain simultaneously strengthens important memories and weakens non-essential ones during sleep—an essential mechanism that enables us to absorb new learning content daily.
conditions: Patients with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy

interventions.name: REM-theta-tCS: experimental nocturnal sleep with cathodal REM-specific theta-tCS in healthy older volunteers (6 Hz, between 5 and 255 μA, DC baseline at 130 μA, 1 s fade in/out, maximum current density 0.507 mA/cm² , duration 5 min with 1-min inter-block intervals). Study part 1.
Sham Stimulation: Sham REM-specific theta-tCS during nocturnal sleep in healthy older volunteers (cross-over assignment, applicable for each participant). Study part 1.

REM-theta-tCS: experimental nocturnal sleep with cathodal REM-specific theta-tCS in healthy older volunteers and epilepsy patients (6 Hz, between 5 and 255 μA, DC baseline at 130 μA, 1 s fade in/out, maximum current density 0.507 mA/cm² , duration 5 min with 1-min inter-block intervals). Will be use

NREM-tCS: experimental nocturnal sleep with NREM-tCS in healthy older volunteers and epilepsy patients (anodal 0.75 Hz, between 5 und 255 μA, DC baseline at 130 μA, maximum current density 0.522 mA/cm2, duration 5 min); study part 2.

Sham Stimulation: Sham REM-specific theta-tCS during nocturnal sleep in healthy older volunteers and epilepsy patients (cross-over assignment, applicable for each participant). Will be used in the crossover block with three conditions in study part 2.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy older adults aged between 60-80 years
- screening in a structured telephone interview
- Epilepsy patients: >18 years of age with drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy
- Epilepsy patients: will undergo intracranial electroencephalography as part of their clinical pre-surgical evaluation of refractory focal epilepsy with a suspected temporal / temporomesial seizure onset zone
- Only participants with health insurance will be included, to ensure that incidental
findings can be further investigated
Exclusion criteria:
Healthy older adults:
- Neurodegenerative neurological illnesses, epilepsy or history of seizures
- medication acting primarily on the central nervous system
- Mini Mental Status Examination scores below 24
- Severe and untreated medical conditions
- History of severe alcoholism or use of drugs
- Severe psychiatric disorders such as depression (if not in remission) or psychosis
- Contraindication to tDCS application
- Sleep disorders (and sleep medication)
- insufficient German language skills (relevant for memory testing)
- the following will not lead to exclusion in the epilepsy patient group: temporal sclerosis; medication acting primarily on the central nervous system

Additional exclusion criteria for epilepsy patients:
- 3 ASD currently taken
- severe cognitive side effects of ASD (EPITRACK with a cutoff score ≤ 28)
